blocks.text: The best way to learn to interpret IR spectra is to study worked examples and become familiar with the characteristic features of a spectrum.

blocks.title: Example 29.1
blocks.text: Two spectra belong to propan-2-ol and propanone. A strong, sharp absorption at about 1710 cm-1 shows a C=O (carbonyl) group, the functional group of a ketone, so spectrum A is propanone. A strong absorption around 3200-3600 cm-1 in spectrum B shows an alcohol -OH group, so B is propan-2-ol.

blocks.alt: Two infrared spectra, A (top) and B (bottom), each plotted as absorbance / % (0 at the top, 100 at the bottom) against wavenumber/cm^-1 from 4000 to 500. A has a small dip near 3450, a strong band near 3000 and a very strong, sharp band near 1750, then several bands below 1500. B has a very broad, deep band centred near 3350, strong bands near 2950 and many bands below 1500.
blocks.caption: Example 29.1: infrared spectra A and B (original drawing after the spectra printed with Example 29.1).
